name: Two-period slope chart
reader_question: How did each item move between two observations, and did any item change rank?
relationship: Per-item change between two observations of one measure; line slope shows direction and relative movement, crossings show rank changes.
use_when: Each item has a value at exactly two comparable cut-offs
Rank changes and direction matter more than exact differences
avoid_when: More than two observations exist — use annotated-line or small-multiples
The reader must compare exact magnitudes or gaps — use dumbbell on a zero-based axis

data_contract.notes: The two observation labels; must differ

units: One unit and basis at both cut-offs; vertical position is linear in value between the lowest and highest value shown, with no zero baseline, and the slide says so.

editable: Lines, end dots and labels as native shapes and text
not_data_bound: Line endpoints are drawn on a computed scale; values are not data-bound and there is no embedded workbook
End labels are separated vertically by a fixed minimum gap, so a label can sit slightly off its dot
Editing a value means moving the line end and rewriting its label

table_alternative: A table of item, first value, second value and change.
variations: Dumbbell for exact gaps on a zero-based axis
Slope with a dashed line for items measured on a different basis
limitations: The vertical scale is not zero-based, so slopes compare direction, not proportional change
Up to eight lines before end labels crowd

excluded_alternatives.reason: Hides rank crossings and makes direction harder to see across many items
Shows rank only and discards the size of the movement
